title: NEW YORK, NY \/ ACCESSWIRE \/ January 8, 2018 \/
text:
NEW YORK, NY \/ ACCESSWIRE \/ January 8, 2018 \/ There were two major chip vulnerabilities revealed last week and Apple has confirmed that it is affected by the flaws. The company said that a recent update has mitigates on one flaw, but the other flaw affects all Mac and iOs devices, but not the iWatch. Shares of Barnes and Noble sank to a new low on Friday as the company turned in disappointing holiday quarter results. \n

Apple Inc. shares closed up 1.14% on about 23.6 million shares traded. It was last week that reports revealed two major chip security flaws, called Meltdown and Spectre, which are affecting companies like NVIDIA and Intel. Apple also confirmed week that all of its Mac computers and iOS devices including iPhones and iPads are also affected but a recent update mitigates the Meltdown vulnerability. The iWatch is not affected by the vulnerabilities as it runs on a different derivative. The company also reassured however that there are no known exploits that are impacting users. Apple said it will release an update to its Safari web browser in the very near future to defend against the Spectre flaw. According to Apple, the steps could slow browser speed by less than 2.5%. \n

Barnes & Noble, Inc. shares sank deep into the red this past Friday, closing the day down nearly 14%. The stock was even dragged to a new 52-week low of $5.40 during intra-day trading after the company revealed a very difficult holiday quarter. The books retailer revealed last week that for the period ended December 30th, 2017, total sales for the nine-week holiday period came out to $953 million. This was a 6.4% year over year decline. Comparable sales declined 6.4% and online sales fell 4.5%. According to the company half of the decline in its sales was due to lower music sales and less people opting to purchase DVDs. The company tried to remain optimistic by stating that it \"remains focused on executing its strategic turnaround plan, including testing the addition of alcohol and coffee products in some locations.\" \n
